pointers.sentence: `partialdef_func`, the compile function of `{% partialdef %}`, reads a name and, optionally, `"inline"`, parses the nodes up to `{% endpartialdef %}`, and wraps them in a `PartialTemplate` with the parser's origin (`django/template/defaulttags.py:partialdef_func`).
When the parse succeeds, `Template.compile_nodelist` keeps the parser's `extra_data` whole as `Template.extra_data` (`django/template/base.py:Template.compile_nodelist`).
It renders nothing unless the tag said `"inline"`, and then renders the fragment in place (`django/template/defaulttags.py:PartialDefNode`).

It gives the `PartialNode` a `DeferredSubDict` over the parser's extra data and the key `"partials"`, which looks up both keys only when it is indexed, so that, as its docstring says, later updates are seen (`django/template/defaulttags.py:partial_func`, `django/utils/datastructures.py:DeferredSubDict`).

It gives the `PartialNode` a `DeferredSubDict` over the parser's extra data and the key `"partials"`, which looks up both keys only when it is indexed, so that, as its docstring says, later updates are seen (`django/template/defaulttags.py:partial_func`, `django/utils/datastructures.py:DeferredSubDict`).
A name the template does not define is a `TemplateSyntaxError`, raised at render: the partial "is not defined in the current template" (`django/template/defaulttags.py:PartialNode.render`).
A `PartialTemplate` gives a partial the shape of a compiled template (`django/template/base.py:PartialTemplate`), so that, its docstring says, it can bind a context.

`PartialTemplate.render` repeats `Template.render`: it pushes a level onto the render context and, if the context is bound to no template, binds it to the partial (`django/template/base.py:PartialTemplate.render`, [Rendering: nodes and the render context](rendering.md)).

`PartialTemplate.source`, and `PartialTemplate.get_exception_info`, which gives an error raised during `PartialTemplate.render` its excerpt for the debug page, fetch the whole template again from the origin's loader and work on its source (`django/template/base.py:PartialTemplate.get_exception_info`, [Template errors and debug information](debugging.md)).

It finds and compiles the part before as any template, and if there is a part after, returns the `PartialTemplate` filed under it in `Template.extra_data` in place of the template (`django/template/engine.py:Engine.get_template`).

Before returning a partial the method sets the engine on it: the parser gives it none, and rendering reads the engine from the template a context is bound to, for, among other things, the context processors and the `"debug"` option (`django/template/context.py:RequestContext.bind_template`, `django/template/base.py:Node.render_annotated`).

The form works wherever a name reaches `Engine.get_template`: in `Engine.select_template`, which calls it on the names in turn until one loads and is what `{% include %}` loads through (`django/template/loader_tags.py:IncludeNode.render`); and in the `DjangoTemplates` backend, which wraps a partial as it wraps a template (`django/template/backends/django.py:DjangoTemplates.get_template`), and with it `render_to_string`, the `render` shortcut and `TemplateResponse`.

`{% extends %}` does not: it calls `Engine.find_template`, which looks for a file named with the whole name, `"#"` and all (`django/template/loader_tags.py:ExtendsNode.find_template`).

The cached loader keeps a template under the part before `"#"`, so a template loaded whole and its partials loaded by name share one compiled template (`django/template/loaders/cached.py:Loader.get_template`).
